what: Yogic vocabulary and images: sahaj, śūnya/sunn, the unstruck sound, the tenth door, the sky-circle with dripping nectar, iḍā–piṅgalā–suṣumnā, unmanī, the 'avadhū' address, upside-down speech

evidence.detail: The Sant songs use the Nāth terms while redirecting them to devotion to the Name.
Kabīr addresses the avadhū (Nāth yogī) and satirizes his garb.
The Kabīr–Gorakh goṣṭhī stages the encounter.

what: The name of Rām as the saving Name; the claim of initiation of Kabīr, Ravidās, Pīpā, Sen and Dhannā by Rāmānanda

evidence.detail: Chronological doubts about direct discipleship (metadata only).

notes: The Kabīr Panth denies dependence; see dsp:kabir-guru-ramananda.

what: Nāmdev's Hindi padas and his example as a low-caste devotee saved by the Name

evidence.detail: Ravidās names Nāmdev among those the Lord saved.
Nāmdev's Hindi songs stand with Kabīr's and Ravidās's in the Pañcvāṇī and Ādi Granth.

what: The older Sants (Kabīr, Paltū, Dariyā, Tulsī Sāhib) as authorities for the inner sound and the Name; their vocabulary of śabd, surat, sunn, tenth door

evidence.detail: Sār Bachan and the Beas and Ruhani Satsang literature quote the older Sants extensively.

what: The cosmology of Kāl and the Sat Puruṣ/Satlok and the sense of the Saints' mission to free souls from Kāl

evidence.detail: Kāl, Sat Puruṣ, Sat Lok in both; the Anurāg Sāgar translated and published in the Sant Mat milieu (Sant Bani Ashram).

what: Nirañjan as the name of the ultimate and Nāth yogic practice

evidence.detail: The sect's name and its 'alakh nirañjan' theology.

what: Sahaja as the innate goal, the body as microcosm, the union of the two principles (prajñā–upāya → Rādhā–Kṛṣṇa), songs in coded language

evidence.detail: S. B. Dasgupta (Obscure Religious Cults) and others trace the Vaiṣṇava Sahajiyā to the Buddhist Sahajiyā of the Caryāgīti (metadata only).
sahaja, sandhyā-bhāṣā, the body as the site of union (cf. src:caryagiti, src:dohakosa-saraha).
The Sahajiyās themselves claim descent from Caitanya and the Vaiṣṇava rasikas, not from Buddhists.

what: Rūpa Gosvāmī's rasa theory, the parakīyā ideal, Caitanya as Rādhā–Kṛṣṇa in one body, the Caitanya-caritāmṛta's kāma/prema distinction

evidence.detail: Sahajiyā texts cite and re-read the Caitanya-caritāmṛta (Vivartavilāsa).

notes: The Gauḍīya tradition rejects the Sahajiyā reading (dsp:sahajiya-and-gaudiya-orthodoxy).

what: Sahaja and the sahaja Man, the body as the place of the divine couple, rasa and rati, the practice of the couple, coded song

evidence.detail: Bāul songs use the Sahajiyā vocabulary (sahaj mānuṣ, rasa, rati, the moons).

what: Body-yoga vocabulary: reversal (ulṭā), the tenth door, the currents and lotuses, the breath

evidence.detail: Nāth images in Bāul deha-tattva songs.

what: Caitanya, Nityānanda and the Vraja līlā as figures of the songs; nāma-kīrtana; the word bāul itself (Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya 19)
Caitanya as source (Āulcānd as Caitanya returned), Vaiṣṇava vocabulary and kīrtana
The sahaja mānuṣa, secrecy, the living human as the site of the divine
